title: Autoscaler-linked soft throughput guarantee shim and admission controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight shim and admission controller that enforces soft per-tenant throughput guarantees while coordinating with the fleet autoscaler to preserve headroom and avoid oscillations. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation in the routing plane, metrics, and a staged rollout for Dedicated pools.
background: Customers on Dedicated request predictable sustained throughput for SLA-backed routes. Current admission only performs token-bucket checks and global shedding which can either under-provision (causing SLO misses) or overreact to bursts (triggering unnecessary autoscaling). We need a solution that offers probabilistic guarantees (soft guarantees) while integrating with autoscaler signals to reduce thrashing and preserve cost efficiency.
proposed_solution: Build a shim that sits in the ingress routing layer: 1) maintain a per-route short-term throughput budget (windowed) derived from the route's committed QPS and historical consumption; 2) expose a reserve headroom token pool synced with autoscaler suggested capacity and in-flight scale operations; 3) admission decisions combine token budget + predictive short-term forecast to accept, queue, or shed requests with graded responses (delay, 429 with Retry-After, or graceful fallback to compatible cheaper model variant). The autoscaler will publish planned capacity changes and a stable headroom target; the shim will respect that to avoid accepting load that will immediately force scaling. For fairness, implement a hybrid priority algorithm that weights reserve usage by customer tier and recent error budget consumption.
implementation_notes:
- Add a new component in routing plane (go service) with a compact in-memory store keyed by route_id.
- Windowed counters: use 1s resolution, 1m sliding window summary.
- Forecasting: simple exponential smoothing (alpha configurable) for next 15s QPS.
- Headroom integration: read autoscaler RPC with a TTL cache; autoscaler annotates planned adds/removes and target headroom in tokens.
- Offer three admission actions: ALLOW, DELAY (enqueue up to N ms), SHED (return 429). DELAY enqueues into an in-node micro-queue with drop-after timeout.
- Expose runtime flags for conservative/aggressive modes.
- Implement Prometheus metrics and tracing hooks for request-level decision reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Shim prototype routes real test traffic in staging and respects per-route committed throughput within +/-20% for 10m window
Autoscaler integration prevents >50% of scale-up/scale-down oscillations during synthetic burst tests compared to current baseline
End-to-end observability: per-route admission decision tagged in traces and visible in Console dashboard
Graceful degradation: clients receive DELAY responses or 429 with Retry-After with documented behavior in SDKs
Configurable rollout toggles and ability to opt a pool or route out
rollout_plan: Merge prototype behind feature flag and run internal canary on dev-dedicated-pool
Run 72h soak with synthetic mixed workloads (steady + bursts) and compare autoscaler churn metrics
Enable for a small subset of paying customers with monitoring and on-call notified
Iterate on thresholds and forecasting parameters after telemetry review
Gradual ramp to wider Dedicated fleets across regions with final docs and runbook
